sections.h2: Who can sell a house in Waxahachie, and what are the main routes?
sections.html:
Any owner of a Waxahachie house can sell it through an agent listing, a direct sale to a buyer, or a cash purchase by an investor. The right route depends on how much repair work the house needs and how soon you need the money.

Waxahachie is the seat of Ellis County, on Interstate 35E and U.S. Highway 287, about thirty miles south of Dallas. That position matters when you sell, because buyers often compare a Waxahachie house with homes closer to Dallas and weigh the commute. Highway access to Dallas and to the rest of Ellis County is a selling point worth naming in any listing or offer conversation.

  • A listing suits a house in good shape that can wait through showings and a lender's appraisal.
  • A direct sale to a neighbor or relative saves marketing effort but still needs a signed deed and a title company or attorney.
  • A cash sale to an investor fits a house with deferred repairs, tenants, probate questions or a tight deadline.

sections.h2: What makes Waxahachie homes different from other Dallas area houses?
sections.html:
Waxahachie has an unusually old core. The town was laid out in August 1850 as the new county seat, was incorporated on April 28, 1871, and earned the nickname Gingerbread City for the Victorian carpentry on homes built before 1900.

The Texas State Historical Association records about 300 Waxahachie structures on the National Register of Historic Places, including the red sandstone and granite courthouse on the square (completed 1897), the octagonal Chautauqua Auditorium (1902) and the Sims Library (1905). A house in a historic pocket near the square can draw buyers who like period detail, and it can also carry older wiring, plumbing and foundations that an inspection will flag.

Newer subdivisions out toward the highways sit in a different market. If your home was built in recent decades, the buyer pool is mostly commuters and families, and the repair list is usually shorter. Ask a local agent or appraiser which category your street falls into before you set an asking price.

sections.h2: How did Waxahachie's economy shape the housing market?
sections.html:
Waxahachie grew on cotton and rail. The Waxahachie Tap Railroad was chartered in 1875 and running by September 1879, later lines followed, and by 1900 a cotton textile mill had opened. By 1926 the town also made garments, brooms and ice cream, and later decades added cottonseed oil, feed and poultry processing, furniture and fiberglass.

Education added another layer. Trinity University operated in town from 1902 to 1942, Southwestern Bible Institute (later Southwestern Assemblies of God College) took over the grounds in 1943, and Navarro College has a branch there. Those institutions explain the clusters of older rental and student housing near campus areas.

The town also hosts the Scarborough Renaissance Faire and a Christmas parade and tour of homes, which bring visitors each year. Sellers sometimes time a listing around those events so more people see the street. Whether that helps a cash sale is a separate matter, since an investor looks at the house itself.

sections.h2: Do I need a city permit before selling a Waxahachie house?
sections.html:
You do not need a permit just to sell, but any repair work before the sale may need one from the Permitting Division of the city's Building and Community Services Department. The city runs an online Citizen Self-Service portal for applications, payments, inspection scheduling and plan review.

The city's permit page lists separate submittal guides for fences, residential remodels, accessory structures, swimming pools, irrigation and certificates of occupancy. It states that the city has adopted the 2021 International Code Council codes and the 2020 National Electric Code with local amendments, and that construction fees are in Chapter 11 of the City Code of Ordinances.

If a previous owner added a room, deck or pool, ask whether a permit was closed out. Open or missing permits tend to surface when a buyer's lender or inspector asks, and they are easier to fix before you list than after you have a contract.

sections.h2: How are property taxes handled when a Waxahachie house sells?
sections.html:
Taxes on a Waxahachie house are billed through Ellis County channels, and the bill is normally split between the buyer and seller at closing. The Ellis County Tax Office posts its calendar publicly, and the dates below come from that page.

Ellis County Tax Office dates (source: ellistaxoffice.com)
DateWhat happens
October 1Collection period begins and bills are mailed
January 31Last day to pay before the delinquency date
February 1Penalty and interest begin on unpaid taxes
April 30Last day to file an exemption application at the Ellis Appraisal District
May 15Last day to file a protest with the appraisal district
July 1Delinquent accounts go to the tax attorneys, with a collection penalty of up to 20 percent

The tax lien for a given year attaches on January 1, so a buyer's title company will want any unpaid bill cleared at closing. The county tax office, at 302 N. Monroe Street in Waxahachie, can give a payoff figure for a specific account.

sections.h2: What exemptions and recording steps apply to a Waxahachie seller?
sections.html:
A seller who has claimed a homestead exemption loses it at the sale, and the buyer applies for their own. School districts must give a $140,000 homestead exemption, and owners 65 or older or disabled get an added $60,000, according to the Comptroller's exemption page. A buyer who closes after January 1 may be able to claim it for the rest of that year if the prior owner did not.

  • Deeds are recorded with the Ellis County Clerk, the county recorder for the county where the property sits.
  • The deed must be signed and acknowledged before a notary or another authorized officer.
  • Recording fees in the clerk manual start at $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, plus smaller records fees.

Bring a government photo ID, the property's legal description and any loan payoff statement to the title company, so the deed can be drafted correctly the first time.

If your Waxahachie loan is behind, foreclosure sales happen at the auction on the first Tuesday of a month after notice is posted and filed at least 21 days ahead. Selling before that date can avoid the auction, so check the loan paperwork and ask the county clerk where notices are filed.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Waxahachie house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. Texas does not require repairs before a sale, and a cash buyer in Waxahachie can purchase a house in its current condition. Open permits or code issues should still be settled or disclosed, and the buyer's title company will look for unpaid taxes and recorded liens.

faqs.q: Which office handles deeds for a Waxahachie property?
faqs.a: The Ellis County Clerk records deeds for property in Waxahachie, because Texas deeds are filed in the county where the land sits. The clerk will check that the deed is signed and acknowledged before accepting it.

faqs.q: When are Ellis County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills go out around October 1 and are due by January 31. Unpaid balances start collecting penalty and interest on February 1, and July 1 brings referral to the tax attorneys with a penalty of up to 20 percent, per the Ellis County Tax Office.

faqs.q: Does the age of a Waxahachie house affect a sale?
faqs.a: It can. Many houses near the square date from before 1900, and buyers of those homes may ask for inspections of wiring, plumbing and the foundation. Newer subdivision homes usually raise fewer questions. A local appraiser can tell you how your block compares.

faqs.q: What if my Waxahachie house is facing foreclosure?
faqs.a: Contact the lender and a housing counselor right away. Texas foreclosure auctions run on the first Tuesday of the month, after a notice of sale is sent, posted at the courthouse and filed with the county clerk at least 21 days before. A sale that closes before then can pay off the loan.
